artifact.title: A proposed read API
artifact.subtitle: Auth, cache, queue, workers and storage, none of it built
artifact.summary: There is no code for any of this and no repository to point at, so this specification declares no source and carries no citation. That is a complete and legal artifact: the diagram describes an intended system, and the engine reports its evidence layer as not run rather than as passed. Nothing here should be read as a claim about what currently runs.

groups.label: At the edge
groups.summary: What a client touches. Intended, not built.

groups.label: The read path
groups.summary: Would answer from cache wherever it can, and never wait on the write path.

groups.label: The write path
groups.summary: Would own every mutation, and publish what happened rather than call whoever cares.

nodes.label: A client
nodes.summary: Would send a token on every request and expect the same answer from any region.

nodes.label: API gateway
nodes.summary: Would terminate TLS, apply rate limits, and route. It would hold no session state.

nodes.label: Token service
nodes.summary: Would verify tokens and nothing else. Deliberately not the place where permissions live.

nodes.label: Read service
nodes.summary: Would serve every query, and would be the only thing allowed to answer from the cache.

nodes.label: Read cache
nodes.summary: Would hold projections, never authoritative state. Safe to lose entirely.

nodes.label: Projection store
nodes.summary: Would be rebuildable from the event log, which is what makes a cold start survivable.

nodes.label: Write service
nodes.summary: Would own every mutation. The one writer of authoritative state.

nodes.label: Authoritative store
nodes.summary: Would be the single source of truth, and would never be read by the read path directly.

nodes.label: change-events
nodes.summary: Would carry what happened, never what should happen next.

nodes.label: Projector
nodes.summary: Would consume events and maintain projections. Idempotent, so a replay is safe.

nodes.label: Cache invalidator
nodes.summary: Would consume the same events and evict rather than write. Two consumers, one log.

nodes.label: Stale or missing?
nodes.summary: Would decide whether to answer from the cache or fall through to projections.

nodes.label: Answered
nodes.summary: Would be reached from either branch, which is the property worth designing for.

paths.label: A query that hits
paths.note: Four steps and nothing authoritative is read, which is the whole reason the read path exists.

paths.label: A query that misses
paths.note: The same first three steps, then a fall-through to projections rather than to the authoritative store.

paths.label: A mutation, and its wake
paths.note: The write path would publish once and be finished; two independent consumers would then do their own work.

views.label: One log, two consumers
views.note: The projector maintains and the invalidator evicts. Neither would know about the other, and that independence is the design.
